The file passes. WorkshopsService does the work expected of an application-layer service. It builds a domain Workshop entity from a DTO, saves and loads it through the WorkshopRepository interface defined in the domain, maps entities to response DTOs, and throws a DomainError when a workshop is not found. All of that is orchestration.

The file contains no persistence code: no database or ORM calls, no SQL, no storage details. It also contains no transport or HTTP handling (no request or response objects, status codes or route decorators), and it does not embed domain rules that belong in the entity.

Two minor points don't change the result:
- The in-memory `sequence` counter used to generate IDs is fragile, but generating an identifier during a use case is still an application-layer concern, not misplaced persistence.
- `FindOneContextDto` carries an optional `requestId`, which leans towards request context. It is a plain DTO, it is never used, and DTOs belong to the application layer in this model, so it doesn't count as transport logic.
